d2.description: Sequential count of a revisit of the bounding area in the last sent Job Definition Segment, where a Revisit Index of '0' indicates the first revisit.

d3.description: Temporally sequential count of a dwell within the revisit of a particular bounding area for a given job ID.

d4.description: Flag indicating the last dwell of the revisit.

d5.description: Count of the total number of targets reported during this dwell and sent in this Dwell Segment.

d6.description: Elapsed time, expressed in milliseconds, from midnight at the beginning of the day specified in the Reference Time fields (missionRefTime) of the Mission Segment.

d7.description: North-South position of the sensor at the temporal center of the dwell, in degrees.

d8.description: The East-West position of the sensor at the temporal center of the dwell, in degrees East (positive, 0 to 180) or West (negative, 0 to -180) of the Prime Meridian.

d9.description: The altitude of the sensor at temporal center of the dwell, above the WGS 84 ellipsoid, expressed in centimeters.

d10.description: Factor which modifies the value of the reported target latitude (Delta Latitude, field D32.4).

d11.description: Factor which modifies the value of the reported target longitude (Delta Longitude, field D32.5).

d12.description: Standard deviation in the estimated horizontal sensor location at the time of the dwell, measured along the sensor track direction (field D15), in centimeters.

d13.description: Standard deviation in the estimated horizontal sensor location at the time of the dwell, measured orthogonal to the sensor track direction (field D15), in centimeters.

d14.description: Standard deviation of the sensor altitude estimate (field D9), in centimeters.

d15.description: Ground track of the sensor at the time of the dwell, as the angle in degrees (clockwise) from True North.

d16.description: Ground speed of the sensor at the time of the dwell, in millimeters per second.

d17.description: Velocity of the sensor in the vertical direction, in decimeters per second.

d18.description: Standard deviation of the estimate of the sensor track, in degrees.

d19.description: Standard deviation of estimate of the sensor speed, in millimeters per second.

d20.description: Standard deviation of estimate of the sensor vertical velocity, expressed in centimeters per second.

d21.description: Heading of the platform at the time of the dwell, as the angle in degrees (clockwise) from True North to the roll axis of the platform.

d22.description: Pitch angle of the platform at the time of the dwell, in degrees.

d23.description: Roll angle of the platform at the time of the dwell, in degrees.

d24.description: The North-South position of the center of the dwell area, expressed as degrees North (positive) or South (negative) of the Equator.

d25.description: The East-West position of the center of the dwell area, expressed as degrees East (positive, 0 to 180) or West (negative, 0 to -180) of the Prime Meridian.

d26.description: Distance on the earth surface, expressed in kilometers, from the near edge to the center of the dwell area.

d27.description: For dwell based radars, one-half of the 3-dB beamwidth.  For non-dwell based radars, the angle between the beginning of the dwell to the center of the dwell.  Measured in degrees.

d28.description: Rotation of the sensor broadside face about the local vertical axis of the platform, in degrees.

d29.description: Rotation angle of the sensor about the transverse axis of the sensor broadside, in degrees.

d30.description: Rotation angle of the sensor about the transverse axis of the sensor broadside, in degrees.

d31.description: Minimum velocity component, along the line of sight, which can be detected by the sensor, in decimeters per second.

d32.description: Minimum velocity component, along the line of sight, which can be detected by the sensor, in decimeters per second.

h32_4.description: Scatterer’s Doppler index relative to Range-Doppler chip, where increasing index equates to increasing Doppler.

h2.description: Sequential count of a revisit of the bounding area for a given job ID.

h5.description: Sequential index of the associated MTI Report.

h6.description: Number of Range Doppler pixels that exceed target scatterer threshold and are reported in this segment.

h7.description: Number of Range Bins/Samples in a Range Doppler Chip.

h8.description: Number of Doppler bins in a Range-Doppler chip.

h9.description: The Peak Scatter returns the maximum power level (e.g. in milliwatts, or dBm) registered by the sensor.

h10.description: Detection threshold used to isolate significant target scatterer pixels, expressed as power relative to clutter mean in negative quarter-decibels.

h11.description: 3dB range impulse response of the radar, expressed in centimeters.

h12.description: Slant Range pixel spacing after over sampling, expressed in centimeters.

h13.description: 3dB Doppler resolution of the radar, expressed in Hertz.

h14.description: Doppler pixel spacing after over sampling, expressed in Hertz.

h15.description: Center Frequency of the radar in GHz.

h16.description: Enumeration table denoting the compression technique used.

h17.description: Enumeration table indicating the spectral weighting used in the range compression process.

h18.description: Enumeration table indicating the spectral weighting used in the cross-range or Doppler compression process.

h19.description: Initial power of the peak scatterer, expressed in dB.

h20.description: RCS of the peak scatterer, expressed in half-decibels (dB/2).

h21.description: When the RDM does not correlate to a single MTI report index or when the center range bin does not correlate to the center of the dwell; provide the range sample offset in meters from Dwell Center (positive is away from the sensor) of the first scatterer record.

h22.description: When the RDM does not correlate to a single MTI report index or the center doppler bin does not correlate to the doppler centroid of the dwell; Doppler sample value in Hz of the first scatterer record.

h23.description: Enumeration field which designates the type of data being delivered.

h24.description: Flag field to indicate the additional signal processing techniques applied to the data.

h27.description: Number of pixels in the range dimension of the chip.

h30.description: Computed object length based upon HRR profile, in meters.

h31.description: Standard deviation of estimate of the object length, expressed in meters.

MtiJobDefinition_Abridged.description: The means for the platform to pass information pertaining to the sensor job that will be performed and details of the location parameters (terrain elevation model and geoid model) used in the measurement.

j2.description: The type of sensor or the platform.

j3.description: Identifier of the particular variant of the sensor type.

j4.description: Flag field indicating whether filtering has been applied to the targets detected within the dwell area.

j5.description: Priority of this tasking request relative to all other active tasking requests scheduled for execution on the specified platform.

j6.description: North-South position of the first corner (Point A) defining the area for sensor service, expressed as degrees North (positive) or South (negative) of the Equator.

j7.description: East-West position of the first corner (Point A) defining the area for sensor service, expressed as degrees East (positive, 0 to 180) or West (negative, 0 to -180) of the Prime Meridian.

j8.description: North-South position of the second corner (Point B) defining the area for sensor service, expressed as degrees North (positive) or South (negative) of the Equator.

j9.description: East-West position of the second corner (Point B) defining the area for sensor service, expressed as degrees East (positive, 0 to 180) or West (negative, 0 to -180) of the Prime Meridian.

j10.description: North-South position of the third corner (Point C) defining the area for sensor service, expressed as degrees North (positive) or South (negative) of the Equator.

j11.description: East-West position of the third corner (Point C) defining the area for sensor service, expressed as degrees East (positive, 0 to 180) or West (negative, 0 to -180) of the Prime Meridian.

j12.description: North-South position of the fourth corner (Point D) defining the area for sensor service, expressed as degrees North (positive) or South (negative) of the Equator.

j13.description: East-West position of the fourth corner (Point D) defining the area for sensor service, expressed as degrees East (positive, 0 to 180) or West (negative, 0 to -180) of the Prime Meridian.

j14.description: Mode in which the radar will operate for the given job ID.

j15.description: The nominal revisit interval for the job ID, expressed in deciseconds.  Value of zero, indicates that the sensor is not revisiting the previous area.

j16.description: Nominal estimate of the standard deviation in the estimated horizontal (along track) sensor location, expressed in decimeters.   measured along the sensor track direction defined in the Dwell segment.

d32_1.description: Sequential count of this MTI report within the dwell.

d32_2.description: The North-South position of the reported detection, expressed as degrees North (positive) or South (negative) of the Equator.

d32_6.description: Height of the reported detection, referenced to its position above the WGS 84 ellipsoid, in meters.

d32_7.description: The component of velocity for the reported detection, expressed in centimeters per second, corrected for platform motion, along the line of sight between the sensor and the reported detection, where the positive direction is away from the sensor.

d32_8.description: The target wrap velocity permits trackers to un-wrap velocities for targets with line-of-sight components large enough to exceed the first velocity period.  Expressed in centimeters/sec.

d32_9.description: Estimated signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the target return, in decibels.

d32_10.description: The classification of the target (i.e. vehicle, aircraft, …).

d32_11.description: Estimated probability that the target classification field is correctly classified.

d32_12.description: Standard deviation of the estimated slant range of the reported detection, in centimeters.

d32_13.description: Standard deviation of the position estimate, in the cross-range direction, of the reported detection, in decimeters.

d32_14.description: Standard deviation of the estimated geodetic height, in meters.

d32_15.description: Standard deviation of the measured line-of-sight velocity component, in centimeters per second.

d32_16.description: The Truth Tag- Application is the Application Field truncated to 8 bits, from the Entity State Protocol Data Unit (PDU) used to generate the MTI Target.

d32_17.description: The Truth Tag - Entity is the Entity Field from the Entity State PDU used to generate the MTI Target.

d32_18.description: Estimated radar cross section of the target return, in half-decibels.

pointLon.description: WGS-84 longitude of this point obstacle, in degrees. -180 to 180 degrees (negative values west of Prime Meridian).

lineNELon.description: WGS-84 longitude of the northeastern point of the line, in degrees. -180 to 180 degrees (negative values west of Prime Meridian).

lineSWLat.description: WGS-84 latitude of the southwestern point of the line, in degrees. -90 to 90 degrees (negative values south of equator).

segStartPoint.description: ID of the starting point of a line segment.

segEndPoint.description: ID of the end point of a line segment.

segNum.description: Identifies the sequence number of a line segment.

facc.description: FACC (Feature and Attribute Coding Catalog) is a five-character code for encoding real-world entities and objects. The first letter of the code is an alphabetic value from "A" to "Z" which will map to a feature category. The second character will map to a subcategory. Characters three to five are numeric and range from 000 to 999. This value will provide a unit feature type identification within the categories.

featureCode.description: Identifying code for the type of this point obstacle.

featureType.description: Identifying code for the type of this point obstacle.

featureDescription.description: Description of this obstacle, corresponding to the FACC (Feature and Attribute Coding Catalog) value.

wac.description: The World Aeronautical Chart (WAC) identifier for the area in which this obstacle is located.

wacINNR.description: This obstacle's World Area Code installation number (WAC-INNR).

multObs.description: Indicates if the feature has multiple obstructions (e.g. S = Single, M = Multiple, U = Undetermined).

numObs.description: Indicates the number of obstructions associated with a feature.

horizDatumCode.description: Code representing the mathematical model of Earth used to calculate coordinates for this obstacle (e.g. WGS-84, U for undetermined, etc.).  US Forces use the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS-84), but also use maps by allied countries with local datums.

heightAGL.description: The height Above Ground Level (AGL) of the point obstacle in feet.

heightAGLAcc.description: The accuracy of the height Above Ground Level (AGL) value for this point obstacle, in feet.

heightMSL.description: The height Above Mean Sea Level (AMSL) of the point obstacle in feet.

heightMSLAcc.description: The accuracy of the height Above Mean Sea Level (AMSL) value for this point obstacle in feet.

elevation.description: The elevation at the point obstacle's location in feet.

elevationAcc.description: The difference between the assigned elevation of this point and its true elevation, in feet.

horizAcc.description: The difference between the recorded horizontal coordinates of this point obstacle and its true position, in feet.

quality.description: When horizontal and/or vertical accuracy requirements cannot be met because of inadequate source material, this code indicates the quality of the data.

lightingCode.description: Code specifying if this obstacle is lit (e.g. Y = Yes, N = No, U = Unknown).

surfaceMatCode.description: The surface material composition code of this point obstacle.

directivityCode.description: The side or sides of this obstruction feature which produces the greatest reflectivity potential.

validationCode.description: Method used to confirm the existence of this obstacle.

transactionCode.description: The transaction type/code for this obstacle (e.g. "D", "N", "R", "S", "V", "X").

processCode.description: Code denoting the action, review, or process that updated this obstacle.

id.description: Unique identifier of the record, auto-generated by the system.

classificationMarking.description: Classification marking of the data in IC/CAPCO Portion-marked format.

cycleDate.description: Start date of this obstruction data set's currency, in ISO 8601 date-only format.

obstacleType.description: Type of obstacle (e.g. P for point, V for vector, L for line).

externalId.description: Optional obstacle ID from external systems. This field has no meaning within UDL and is provided as a convenience for systems that require tracking of an internal system generated ID.

origId.description: The original ID for this obstacle.

countryCode.description: The DoD Standard Country Code designator for the country issuing the diplomatic clearance. This field will be set to "OTHR" if the source value does not match a UDL Country code value (ISO-3166-ALPHA-2).

provinceCode.description: The Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) state/province numeric code of this obstacle's location.

pointLat.description: WGS-84 latitude of this point obstacle, in degrees. -90 to 90 degrees (negative values south of equator).

pointLon.description: WGS-84 longitude of this point obstacle, in degrees. -180 to 180 degrees (negative values west of Prime Meridian).

lineNELon.description: WGS-84 longitude of the northeastern point of the line, in degrees. -180 to 180 degrees (negative values west of Prime Meridian).

lineNELat.description: WGS-84 latitude of the northeastern point of the line, in degrees. -90 to 90 degrees (negative values south of equator).

lineSWLon.description: WGS-84 longitude of the southwestern point of the line, in degrees. -180 to 180 degrees (negative values west of Prime Meridian).

lineSWLat.description: WGS-84 latitude of the southwestern point of the line, in degrees. -90 to 90 degrees (negative values south of equator).

segStartPoint.description: ID of the starting point of a line segment.

segEndPoint.description: ID of the end point of a line segment.

segNum.description: Identifies the sequence number of a line segment.

facc.description: FACC (Feature and Attribute Coding Catalog) is a five-character code for encoding real-world entities and objects. The first letter of the code is an alphabetic value from "A" to "Z" which will map to a feature category. The second character will map to a subcategory. Characters three to five are numeric and range from 000 to 999. This value will provide a unit feature type identification within the categories.

featureCode.description: Identifying code for the type of this point obstacle.

featureType.description: Identifying code for the type of this point obstacle.

featureDescription.description: Description of this obstacle, corresponding to the FACC (Feature and Attribute Coding Catalog) value.

wac.description: The World Aeronautical Chart (WAC) identifier for the area in which this obstacle is located.

wacINNR.description: This obstacle's World Area Code installation number (WAC-INNR).

multObs.description: Indicates if the feature has multiple obstructions (e.g. S = Single, M = Multiple, U = Undetermined).

numObs.description: Indicates the number of obstructions associated with a feature.

horizDatumCode.description: Code representing the mathematical model of Earth used to calculate coordinates for this obstacle (e.g. WGS-84, U for undetermined, etc.).  US Forces use the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS-84), but also use maps by allied countries with local datums.

heightAGL.description: The height Above Ground Level (AGL) of the point obstacle in feet.

heightAGLAcc.description: The accuracy of the height Above Ground Level (AGL) value for this point obstacle, in feet.

heightMSL.description: The height Above Mean Sea Level (AMSL) of the point obstacle in feet.

heightMSLAcc.description: The accuracy of the height Above Mean Sea Level (AMSL) value for this point obstacle in feet.

elevation.description: The elevation at the point obstacle's location in feet.

elevationAcc.description: The difference between the assigned elevation of this point and its true elevation, in feet.

horizAcc.description: The difference between the recorded horizontal coordinates of this point obstacle and its true position, in feet.

quality.description: When horizontal and/or vertical accuracy requirements cannot be met because of inadequate source material, this code indicates the quality of the data.

lightingCode.description: Code specifying if this obstacle is lit (e.g. Y = Yes, N = No, U = Unknown).

surfaceMatCode.description: The surface material composition code of this point obstacle.

directivityCode.description: The side or sides of this obstruction feature which produces the greatest reflectivity potential.

validationCode.description: Method used to confirm the existence of this obstacle.

transactionCode.description: The transaction type/code for this obstacle (e.g. "D", "N", "R", "S", "V", "X").

processCode.description: Code denoting the action, review, or process that updated this obstacle.

actDelCode.description: Indicates if this obstacle record is Active (A) or Deleted (D).

producer.description: Name of the agency that produced this obstruction data set.

derivingOrg.description: The organization that entered obstacle data other than the producer.

deletingOrg.description: The organization that deleted this obstacle record.

sourceDate.description: Source date of this obstacle data, in ISO 8601 date-only format (ex. YYYY-MM-DD).

revDate.description: Date this obstacle data was revised, in ISO 8601 date-only format (ex. YYYY-MM-DD).

initRecordDate.description: Date this obstacle was initially added to the data set, in ISO 8601 date-only format (ex. YYYY-MM-DD).

keys.description: This field provides an array of keys that can be added to any obstruction feature to provide information that is not already supported. The entries in this array must correspond to the position index in the values array. This array must be the same length as values.

values.description: This field provides an array of values that can be added to any obstruction feature to provide information that is not already supported. The entries in this array must correspond to the position index in the keys array. This array must be the same length as keys.

nextCycleDate.description: The date after which this obstruction data set’s currency is stale and should be refreshed, in ISO 8601 date-only format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DD).

baselineCutoffDate.description: Earliest record date possible in this obstruction data set (not the earliest data item), in ISO 8601 date-only format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DD). If null, this data set is assumed to be a full data pull of holdings until the cutoffDate.  If this field is populated, this data set only contains updates since the last baseline data set.

cutoffDate.description: Latest record date possible in this obstruction data set (not the most recent data item), in ISO 8601 date-only format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DD).

airacCycle.description: The Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control (AIRAC) cycle of this obstruction data set. The format is YYNN where YY is the last two digits of the year and NN is the cycle number.

baseAiracCycle.description: The baseline Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control (AIRAC) cycle for change sets only. The format is YYNN where YY is the last two digits of the year and NN is the cycle number.

ownerCountryCode.description: The DoD Standard Country Code designator for the country or political entity that owns the data set associated with this obstruction. This field will be set to "OTHR" if the source value does not match a UDL Country code value (ISO-3166-ALPHA-2).

boundNELon.description: WGS-84 longitude of the northeastern boundary for obstructions contained in this data set, in degrees. -180 to 180 degrees (negative values west of Prime Meridian).

boundNELat.description: WGS-84 latitude of the northeastern boundary for obstructions contained in this data set, in degrees. -90 to 90 degrees (negative values south of equator).

boundSWLon.description: WGS-84 longitude of the southwestern boundary for obstructions contained in this data set, in degrees. -180 to 180 degrees (negative values west of Prime Meridian).

boundSWLat.description: WGS-84 latitude of the southwestern boundary for obstructions contained in this data set, in degrees. -90 to 90 degrees (negative values south of equator).

minHeightAGL.description: The minimum height Above Ground Level (AGL) of the shortest obstruction contained in this data set, in feet.

numPoints.description: The number of point features associated with this obstruction data set.

numLines.description: The number of line features associated with this obstruction data set.

dataSetRemarks.description: Remarks concerning this obstruction's data set.

pointsFilename.description: The name of the point file associated with this obstruction data set.

linesFilename.description: The name of the line file associated with this obstruction data set.

vectorsFilename.description: The name of the vector file associated with this obstruction data set.

ObjectOfInterest_Abridged.description: OnOrbit objects of interest, which include information about the last known state of the object.

id.description: Unique identifier of the record, auto-generated by the system.

classificationMarking.description: Classification marking of the data in IC/CAPCO Portion-marked format.

idOnOrbit.description: UUID of the parent Onorbit record.

satNo.description: Satellite/Catalog number of the target on-orbit object.

name.description: Unique name of the object of interest event.

sensorTaskingStartTime.description: Sensor tasking start time for object of interest.

sensorTaskingStopTime.description: Sensor tasking stop time for object of interest.

priority.description: Priority of the object of interest as an integer (1=highest priority).

status.description: Status of the object of interest event (e.g. OPEN, CLOSED, CANCELLED).

statusDate.description: Time of last status change of the object of interest event.

description.description: Description of the object of interest event.

lastObTime.description: Last reported observation time in ISO 8601 UTC time, with microsecond precision.

missedObTime.description: The time at which an attempted observation of the object of interest noticed it was missing, in ISO 8601 UTC time, with microsecond precision.

deltaVs.description: Possible delta V applications for the object of interest, in km/sec.

deltaTs.description: Possible delta time applications for the object of interest, in seconds.

svEpoch.description: Last reported state vector epoch time in ISO 8601 UTC time, with microsecond precision.

x.description: Last reported x position of the object in km, in J2000 coordinates.

y.description: Last reported y position of the object in km, in J2000 coordinates.

z.description: Last reported z position of the object in km, in J2000 coordinates.

xvel.description: Last reported x velocity of the object in km/sec, in J2000 coordinates.

yvel.description: Last reported y velocity of the object in km/sec, in J2000 coordinates.

zvel.description: Last reported z velocity of the object in km/sec, in J2000 coordinates.

elsetEpoch.description: Last reported elset epoch time in ISO 8601 UTC time, with microsecond precision.

meanMotion.description: Last reported mean motion of the object. Mean motion is the angular speed required for a body to complete one orbit, assuming constant speed in a circular orbit which completes in the same time as the variable speed, elliptical orbit of the actual body. Measured in revolutions per day.

eccentricity.description: Last reported eccentricity of the object. The orbital eccentricity of an astronomical object is a parameter that determines the amount by which its orbit around another body deviates from a perfect circle. A value of 0 is a circular orbit, values between 0 and 1 form an elliptic orbit, 1 is a parabolic escape orbit, and greater than 1 is a hyperbolic escape orbit.

inclination.description: Last reported inclination of the object. Inclination is the angle between the equator and the orbit when looking from the center of the Earth. If the orbit went exactly around the equator from left to right, then the inclination would be 0. The inclination ranges from 0 to 180 degrees.

raan.description: Last reported raan.  Right ascension of the ascending node, or RAAN is the angle as measured in degrees eastwards (or, as seen from the north, counterclockwise) from the First Point of Aries to the ascending node, which is where the orbit crosses the equator when traveling north.

argOfPerigee.description: Last reported argument of perigee. The argument of perigee is the angle in degrees formed between the perigee and the ascending node. If the perigee would occur at the ascending node, the argument of perigee would be 0.

meanAnomaly.description: Last reported meanAnomaly. Mean anomoly is where the satellite is in its orbital path. The mean anomaly ranges from 0 to 360 degrees. The mean anomaly is referenced to the perigee. If the satellite were at the perigee, the mean anomaly would be 0.

revNo.description: The last reported revolution number. The value is incremented when a satellite crosses the equator on an ascending pass.

bStar.description: Last reported drag term for SGP4 orbital model, used for calculating decay constants for altitude, eccentricity etc, measured in inverse earth radii.

meanMotionDot.description: Last reported 1st derivative of the mean motion with respect to time. Units are revolutions per day squared.

meanMotionDDot.description: Last reported 2nd derivative of the mean motion with respect to time. Units are revolutions per day cubed.

semiMajorAxis.description: Last reported semi major axis, which is the sum of the periapsis and apoapsis distances divided by two. For circular orbits, the semimajor axis is the distance between the centers of the bodies, not the distance of the bodies from the center of mass.

period.description: Last reported orbit period. Period of the orbit is equal to inverse of mean motion.

apogee.description: Last reported apogee. The Orbit point furthest from the center of the earth in kilometers.

perigee.description: Last reported perigee. The orbit point nearest to the center of the earth in kilometers.

createdBy.description: Application user who created the row in the database, auto-populated by the system.

origin.description: Originating system or organization which produced the data, if different from the source. meanMotionDDot.description: Last reported 2nd derivative of the mean motion with respect to time. Units are revolutions per day cubed.

semiMajorAxis.description: Last reported semi major axis, which is the sum of the periapsis and apoapsis distances divided by two. For circular orbits, the semimajor axis is the distance between the centers of the bodies, not the distance of the bodies from the center of mass.

period.description: Last reported orbit period. Period of the orbit is equal to inverse of mean motion.

apogee.description: Last reported apogee. The Orbit point furthest from the center of the earth in kilometers.

perigee.description: Last reported perigee. The orbit point nearest to the center of the earth in kilometers.

affectedObjects.description: Optional array of Onorbit IDs (idOnOrbit) representing satellites potentially affected by this object of interest.

ObsCorrelation_Abridged.description: Model representation supporting post-pass correlation of UCTs and re-correlation of mis-tagged electro-optical (EO), radar, RF, and DOA track/observations.

id.description: Unique identifier of the record, auto-generated by the system.

classificationMarking.description: Classification marking of the data in IC/CAPCO Portion-marked format.

msgTs.description: Correlation message generation time, in ISO 8601 UTC format with millisecond precision.

corrType.description:
Indicator of whether the type of correlation is OBSERVATION or TRACK:
OBSERVATION: Identifies an observation is being correlated.
TRACK: Identifies the entire track of observations is being correlated.

obType.description:
Indicator of whether the type of Observation(s) being correlated is DOA, EO, PASSIVE_RADAR, RADAR, RF, SAR, or SOISET:
DOA: The observation type being correlated is Difference of Arrival.
EO: The observation type being correlated is Electro-Optical.
PASSIVE_RADAR: The observation type being correlated is Passive Radar.
RADAR: The observation type being correlated is Radar.
RF: The observation type being correlated is Radio Frequency.
SAR: The observation type being correlated is Synthetic Aperture Radar.
SOISET: The observation type being correlated is Space Object Identification Observation Set.

obId.description: Identifier of the Observation associated with this Correlation. If corrType=TRACK then this field should reference the first Observation in the track. Note: To retrieve all remaining Observations in the track, the GET query should include this Observation's source and origin field values, along with the trackId.

idParentCorrelation.description: Identifier of the ObsCorrelation record from which this ObsCorrelation record originated. This behavior allows for different source providers/systems to make changes to a given correlation and maintain traceability back to the original correlation.

trackId.description: Identifier of the Track associated with this ObsCorrelation.

referenceOrbitId.description: Identifier of the orbit state used for correlation.

referenceOrbitType.description:
Indicator of whether the reference orbit type used for correlation is an ELSET, ESID, or SV:
ELSET: The reference orbit type is an Element Set.
ESID: The reference orbit type is an Ephemeris Set.
SV: The reference orbit type is a State Vector.

algorithmCorrType.description: Type of algorithm used for this correlation (e.g. ROTAS, GEOMETRIC, STATISTICAL, MAHALANOBIS, AI/ML, OTHER).

corrQuality.description: Correlation score ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. A score of 1.0 represents perfect correlation to the orbit of the corresponding satellite, such as when all observation residuals equal 0.

astat.description: Astrostandard ROTAS correlation result (0 - 4), if applicable.  Refer to ROTAS documentation for an explanation of ASTAT values.

satNo.description: Current 18th SDS satellite/catalog number of the target on-orbit object. Useful to know in the case where an observation is correlated to another satellite/catalog number.

origObjectId.description: Optional identifier indicates the target on-orbit object being correlated. This may be an internal identifier and not necessarily a valid satellite number.

idOnOrbit.description: Identifier of the correlated target on-orbit object, if associated with a valid satNo.

altNamespace.description: Associates one or more alternate catalogs with a source provider or system. Namespaces may be defined by their respective data providers or systems (e.g. JCO, 18SDS, EOSSS, EXO, KBR, KRTL, LeoLabs, NorthStar, SAFRAN, Slingshot).

altObjectId.description: Alternate unique object ID within the namespace.

altUct.description: Boolean indicating whether the observation or track can be correlated to the alternate object specified under altObjectId. This flag should only be set to true by data providers after an attempt to correlate to an on-orbit object was made and failed. If unable to correlate, the 'origObjectId' field may be populated with an internal data provider specific identifier.

transactionId.description: Optional identifier to track a commercial or marketplace transaction executed to produce this data.

OnboardNavigation_Abridged.description: These services provide spacecraft positional data derived from on-board navigational sensors.  Navigational points are provided in kilometers and in a user specified reference frame, with ECI J2K being preferred.

id.description: Unique identifier of the record, auto-generated by the system.

classificationMarking.description: Classification marking of the data in IC/CAPCO Portion-marked format.

idOnOrbit.description: Unique identifier of the primary satellite on-orbit object.

satNo.description: Satellite/catalog number of the target on-orbit object.

origObjectId.description: Optional identifier provided by the data source to indicate the target object of this record. This may be an internal identifier and not necessarily map to a valid satellite number.

startTime.description: Start time of the sensor data, in ISO 8601 UTC format.

endTime.description: End time of the sensor data, in ISO 8601 UTC format.

esId.description: Unique identifier of the parent EphemerisSet, if this data is correlated with an Ephemeris.  If multiple nav sensor records are required, this ID may be associated with each of those records if each is synced to the ephemeris points.

starCatName.description: The name or identifier the star catalog in use.

starCatLoadTime.description: The last load time of the current star catalog onboard this spacecraft.

idStateVector.description: Unique identifier of the last onboard state vector.

ts.description: Array of epochs of the observations, in ISO 8601 UTC format.  The epochs are assumed to correspond to all sensor data in this record.  If sensors do not share a common epoch then separate records should be generated.

referenceFrame.description: The reference frame in which the sensor derived positions are provided. If the referenceFrame is null it is assumed to be J2000.  Note that this frame is assumed to apply to all of the sensor data in this record.  If onboard sensors process positional estimates in different frames then separate records should be generated.

sunSensor.description: Arrays of spacecraft position (X, Y, Z), in km, in the specified referenceFrame, based on the onboard sun sensor, at each epoch.

mag.description: Arrays of spacecraft position (X, Y, Z), in km, in the specified referenceFrame, based on the onboard magnetometer, at each epoch.

starTracker.description: Arrays of spacecraft position (X, Y, Z), in km, in the specified referenceFrame, based on the onboard star tracker, at each epoch.

deltaPos.description: Arrays of spacecraft delta position (X, Y, Z), in km, in the specified referenceFrame, between the onboard state and the last accepted sensor position.

REAL: Data collected or produced that pertains to real-world objects, events, and analysis.

TEST: Specific datasets used to evaluate compliance with specifications and requirements, and for validating technical, functional, and performance characteristics.

EXERCISE: Data pertaining to a government or military exercise. The data may include both real and simulated data.

SIMULATED: Synthetic data generated by a model to mimic real-world datasets.

origNetwork.description: The originating source network on which this record was created, auto-populated by the system.

OnorbitAssessment_Abridged.description: Spacecraft characterization results from analysis of MASINT data. Supports results of both the overall assessment of a particular spacecraft as well as of individual signature packages.

id.description: Unique identifier of the record, auto-generated by the system.

classificationMarking.description: Classification marking of the data in IC/CAPCO Portion-marked format.

assmtTime.description: The time of the assessment, in ISO 8601 UTC format with millisecond precision.

obTime.description: The observation time, in ISO 8601 UTC format with millisecond precision. For non-instantaneous collections, the observation time will correspond to the earliest timestamp in the signature or signature set data.

obDuration.description: The total duration, in hours, of the signature or set of signatures used to create this assessment.

satNo.description: Satellite/Catalog number of the target on-orbit object to which this assessment applies.

idOnOrbit.description: Unique identifier of the target satellite on-orbit object to which this assessment applies. This ID can be used to obtain additional information on an OnOrbit object using the 'get by ID' operation (e.g. /udl/onorbit/{id}). For example, the OnOrbit with idOnOrbit = 25544 would be queried as /udl/onorbit/25544.

origObjectId.description: Optional identifier provided by the source to indicate the target on-orbit object to which this assessment applies. This may be an internal identifier and not necessarily map to a valid satellite number.

idSensor.description: Unique identifier of the sensor from which the signature data applied in this assessment was collected. This ID can be used to obtain additional information on a sensor using the 'get by ID' operation (e.g. /udl/sensor/{id}). For example, the sensor with idSensor = abc would be queried as /udl/sensor/abc.

origSensorId.description: Optional identifier provided by the observation source to indicate the sensor which produced this observation. This may be an internal identifier and not necessarily a valid sensor ID.

autoAssmt.description: Flag indicating whether this assessment was auto-generated (true) or produced by an analyst.

assmtLevel.description: The level (SATELLITE, SIGNATURE) of this assessment.

assessment.description: The overall assessment of the on-orbit object. The assessment will vary depending on the assessment level. If assmtLevel = SATELLITE, then expected values include HEALTHY, NO DATA, UNHEALTHY, and UNKNOWN. If assmtLevel = SIGNATURE, then expected values include ANOMALOUS, BAD, NOMINAL, and UNKNOWN.

assmtSubType.description: The sub-type for this assessment. The sub-type provides an additional level of specification when the assessment level = SIGNATURE, and will vary based on the overall assessment. If assessment = ANOMALOUS, then expected values include ACTIVITY OBSERVED, BAD CONFIGURATION, MANEUVERING, OTHER, POSSIBLE SAFE MODE, UNSTABLE, and WRONG ATTITUDE. If assessment = BAD, then expected values include BAD-MISSING STATE VECTOR, CORRUPT-NOISY, CROSS-TAG, DROPOUTS, INSUFFICIENT DATA, INSUFFICIENT LOOK ANGLE, NO CROSSOVER, and SHORT. If assessment = NOMINAL, then expected values include ACTIVITY OBSERVED, GRAVITY GRADIENT, HORIZON STABLE, INERTIAL, MANEUVERING, SPIN STABLE, and STABLE. If assessment = UNKNOWN, then expected values include NO COHORT, and OTHER.

assmtDetails.description: Comments and details concerning this assessment.
assmtDetails.example: This spacecraft appears to be in a stable, 3-axis controlled state

assmtRotPeriod.description: The rotational period, in seconds, determined in the assessment of the on-orbit object.

sigDataType.description: The observation data type (LONG DWELL, NARROWBAND, PHOTOMETRIC POL, PHOTOMETRY, RANGE PROFILER, WIDEBAND, etc.) contained in the signature. Applies when assmtLevel = SIGNATURE.

srcTyps.description: Array of UDL record types (DOA, ELSET, EO, ESID, GROUNDIMAGE, POI, MANEUVER, MTI, RADAR, RF, SIGACT, SKYIMAGE, SV, TRACK, etc.) that are related to this assessment. See the associated 'srcIds' array for the record UUIDs, positionally corresponding to the record types in this array. The 'srcTyps' and 'srcIds' arrays must match in size.

srcIds.description: Array of UUIDs of the UDL data records that are related to this assessment. See the associated 'srcTyps' array for the specific types of data, positionally corresponding to the UUIDs in this array. The 'srcTyps' and 'srcIds' arrays must match in size. See the corresponding srcTyps array element for the data type of the UUID and use the appropriate API operation to retrieve that object.

components.description: Array of the affected spacecraft component(s) relevant to this assessment, if non-nominal.

collectionURL.description: URL to an external location containing the data that was used to make this assessment.

assmtURL.description: URL to an external location containing additional assessment information.

transactionId.description: Optional identifier to track a commercial or marketplace transaction executed to produce this data.

createdAt.description: Time the row was created in the database, auto-populated by the system.

createdBy.description: Application user who created the row in the database, auto-populated by the system.

sourceDL.description: The source data library from which this record was received. This could be a remote or tactical UDL or another data library. If null, the record should be assumed to have originated from the primary Enterprise UDL.

origin.description: Originating system or organization which produced the data, if different from the source. The origin may be different than the source if the source was a mediating system which forwarded the data on behalf of the origin system. If null, the source may be assumed to be the origin.

origNetwork.description: The originating source network on which this record was created, auto-populated by the system.

OnorbitListItem_Full.description: Items associated with this onOrbitList record.

origObjectId.description: Optional identifier indicates the on-orbit object being referenced. This may be an internal system identifier and not necessarily a valid satellite number.

objectId.description: Unique identifier of the on-orbit object. This is typically the USSF 18th SDS satellite number (also sometimes referred to as NORAD ID/number) but could be an identifier from another satellite catalog namespace. See the ‘namespace’ field for the appropriate identifier namespace. If namespace is null, 18SDS satellite number is assumed.

commonName.description: Common name of the onorbit object.

countryCode.description: This value is typically the ISO 3166 Alpha-3 three-character country code, however it can also represent various consortiums that do not appear in the ISO document.

orbitRegime.description: Orbit Regime refers to a classification of a satellite's orbit based on its altitude, inclination, and other orbital characteristics. Common orbit regimes include Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), Geostationary Orbit (GEO), and Highly Elliptical Orbit (HEO).

rank.description: Rank refers to the assigned position or level of priority given to a satellite based on its relative importance, urgency, or operational relevance as determined by the applicable operations unit.

urgency.description: Tasking urgency, typically will be on a 1-10 scale.  Urgency as a number. (1=highest priority).

payloadPriority.description: Payload priority based on the type of payload that has been identified or that is suspected. Priority of the payload as a number. (1=highest priority).

monitoringType.description: Routine tasking that should be applied to this object.  REVISIT_RATE allows users to define custom revisit rates for individual satellites, HVA_CLEARING allows users to define custom volumes that are expected to be clear of unknown objects, and POL would be collects on a specified increment in support of collecting data that feeds into Pattern of Life (PoL) assessments.

freqMins.description: Frequency of additional routine, in minutes, tasking identified in and corresponding to the monitoringType array.

clearingRadius.description: Radius, in degrees, of a spherical volume expected to be cleared by sensor providers, if CLEARING is selected.

clearingBoxInTrack.description: Width of a box volume, in degrees, expected to be cleared by sensor providers, if CLEARING is selected.

clearingBoxCrossTrack.description: Height of a box, in degrees, volume expected to be cleared by sensor providers, if CLEARING is selected.

expiredOn.description: Datetime expiration of a satellite on this list, allowing for the maintenance of a history of when satellites entered and when they exited the list in ISO 8601 UTC datetime format with millisecond precision.

The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

eval.description: The Intelligence Confidence Level or the Reliability/degree of confidence that the analyst has assigned to the data within this record. The numerical range is from 1 to 9 with 1 representing the highest confidence level.

fpa.description: Functional Production Area (FPA) under the Shared Production Program (SPP). Producers are defined per country per FPA.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

ident.description:
Estimated identity of the Site (ASSUMED FRIEND, FRIEND, HOSTILE, FAKER, JOKER, NEUTRAL, PENDING, SUSPECT, UNKNOWN): 

ASSUMED FRIEND: Track assumed to be a friend due to the object characteristics, behavior, and/or origin.

FRIEND: Track object supporting friendly forces and belonging to a declared friendly nation or entity.

HOSTILE: Track object belonging to an opposing nation, party, group, or entity deemed to contribute to a threat to friendly forces or their mission due to its behavior, characteristics, nationality, or origin.

FAKER: Friendly track, object, or entity acting as an exercise hostile.

JOKER: Friendly track, object, or entity acting as an exercise suspect.

NEUTRAL: Track object whose characteristics, behavior, nationality, and/or origin indicate that it is neither supporting nor opposing friendly forces or their mission.

PENDING: Track object which has not been evaluated.

SUSPECT: Track object deemed potentially hostile due to the object characteristics, behavior, nationality, and/or origin.

UNKNOWN: Track object which has been evaluated and does not meet criteria for any standard identity.

allegiance.description: The DoD Standard country code designator for the country or political entity to which the operating unit owes its allegiance.  This field will be set to "OTHR" if the source value does not match a UDL country code value (ISO-3166-ALPHA-2).

altAllegiance.description: Specifies an alternate allegiance code if the data provider code is not part of an official Country Code standard such as ISO-3166 or FIPS. This field will be set to the value provided by the source and should be used for all Queries specifying allegiance.

locReason.description: Indicates the reason that the operating unit is at that location.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

force.description: An aggregation of military units within a single service (i.e., ARMY, AIR FORCE, etc.) which operates under a single authority to accomplish a common mission. The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

forceName.description: The specific name for a given force.  For example, Force = ADF (Air Defense Force) and Force Name = Army Air Defense Force.

functRole.description: Principal combat-related role that an operating unit is organized, structured and equipped to perform.  Or, the specialized military or paramilitary branch in which an individual serves, their specialization.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

msnPrimary.description: Indicates the principal type of mission that an operating unit is organized and equipped to perform.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

msnPrimarySpecialty.description: Indicates the principal specialty type of mission that an operating unit is organized and equipped to perform.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

masterUnit.description: This field contains a value indicating whether the record is a master unit record (True) or a detail record (False).  Master records contain basic information that does not change over time for each unit that has been selected to be projected.

stylizedUnit.description: This field contains a value indicating whether the record is a stylized operating unit record (True) or a regular operating unit  record (False).  A stylized operating unit is a type of operating unit with one set of equipment that can be assigned to one or more superiors.  A stylized operating unit is generally useful for lower echelon operating units where the number of operating units and types of equipment are equal for multiple organizations.  In lieu of creating unique operating unit records for each operating unit, a template is created for the operating unit and its equipment.  This template enables the user to assign the operating unit to multiple organizations.

divCat.description: Combat status of a divisional or equivalent operating unit.  Currently, this data element applies only to operating units of the Former Soviet Union.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

echelon.description: Organizational level of the operating unit.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

echelonTier.description: Indicates the major group or level to which an echelon belongs.   The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

fleetId.description: Naval fleet to which an operating unit is assigned.   The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

deployStatus.description: A code describing the amount of operating unit participation in a deployment.   The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

US Forces use the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84), but also use maps by allied countries with local datums.  The datum must be specified to ensure accuracy of coordinates.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

Indicates any of the magnitudes that serve to define the position of a point by reference to a fixed figure, system of lines, etc.

Pos. 3-4. Latitude Minutes     [00-59]

Pos. 5-6. Latitude Seconds     [00-59]

Pos. 7-9. Latitude Thousandths Of Seconds     [000-999]

Pos. 10. Latitude Hemisphere     [NS]

Pos. 11-13. Longitude Degrees     [00-180]

Pos. 14-15. Longitude Minutes     [00-59]

milGridSys.description:
Indicates the grid system used in the development of the milGrid coordinates. Values are:

UPS - Universal Polar System

UTM - Universal Transverse Mercator

milGrid.description:
The Military Grid Reference System is the geocoordinate standard used by NATO militaries for locating points on Earth. The MGRS is derived from the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) grid system and the Universal Polar Stereographic (UPS) grid system, but uses a different labeling convention. The MGRS is used as geocode for the entire Earth. Example of an milgrid coordinate, or grid reference, would be 4QFJ12345678, which consists of three parts:
4Q (grid zone designator, GZD)
FJ (the 100,000-meter square identifier)
12345678 (numerical location; easting is 1234 and northing is 5678, in this case specifying a location with 10 m resolution).

utm.description:

HOSTILE: Track object belonging to an opposing nation, party, group, or entity deemed to contribute to a threat to friendly forces or their mission due to its behavior, characteristics, nationality, or origin.

SUSPECT: Track object deemed potentially hostile due to the object characteristics, behavior, nationality, and/or origin.

UNKNOWN: Track object which has been evaluated and does not meet criteria for any standard identity.

milGrid.description:
The Military Grid Reference System is the geocoordinate standard used by NATO militaries for locating points on Earth. The MGRS is derived from the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) grid system and the Universal Polar Stereographic (UPS) grid system, but uses a different labeling convention. The MGRS is used as geocode for the entire Earth. Example of an milgrid coordinate, or grid reference, would be 4QFJ12345678, which consists of three parts:
4Q (grid zone designator, GZD)
FJ (the 100,000-meter square identifier)
12345678 (numerical location; easting is 1234 and northing is 5678, in this case specifying a location with 10 m resolution).

REAL: Data collected or produced that pertains to real-world objects, events, and analysis.

TEST: Specific datasets used to evaluate compliance with specifications and requirements, and for validating technical, functional, and performance characteristics.

EXERCISE: Data pertaining to a government or military exercise. The data may include both real and simulated data.

SIMULATED: Synthetic data generated by a model to mimic real-world datasets.

Operatingunit_Ingest.description: Model representation of a unit or organization which operates or controls a space-related Entity such as an on-orbit payload, a sensor, etc.  A contact may belong to an organization.

idOperatingUnit.description: Unique identifier of the record, auto-generated by the system.

classificationMarking.description: Classification marking of the data in IC/CAPCO Portion-marked format.

altOperatingUnitId.description: Unique identifier of the operating unit record from the originating system.

description.description: Description of the operating unit.

idLocation.description: Unique identifier of the location record for this operating unit.

idContact.description: Unique identifier of the contact for this operating unit.

idOrganization.description: Unique identifier of the organization record for this operating unit.

unitIdentifier.description: An optional identifier for this operating unit that may be composed from items such as the originating organization, allegiance, one-up number, etc.

countryCode.description: The DoD Standard country code designator for the country or political entity to which the operating unit geographic coordinates reside . This field will be set to "OTHR" if the source value does not match a UDL country code value (ISO-3166-ALPHA-2).

altCountryCode.description: Specifies an alternate country code if the data provider code is not part of an official Country Code standard such as ISO-3166 or FIPS. This field will be set to the value provided by the source and should be used for all Queries specifying a Country Code.

wac.description: World Aeronautical Chart identifier for the area in which a designated operating unit is located.

operStatus.description: The Degree to which an operating unit is ready to perform the overall operational mission(s) for which it was organized and equipped.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

condition.description: The physical manner of being or state of existence of the operating unit.  A physical condition that must be considered in the determining of a course of action.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

conditionAvail.description: Availability of the operating unit relative to its condition.  Indicates the reason the operating unit is not fully operational.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

eval.description: The Intelligence Confidence Level or the Reliability/degree of confidence that the analyst has assigned to the data within this record. The numerical range is from 1 to 9 with 1 representing the highest confidence level.

fpa.description: Functional Production Area (FPA) under the Shared Production Program (SPP). Producers are defined per country per FPA.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

ident.description:
Estimated identity of the Site (ASSUMED FRIEND, FRIEND, HOSTILE, FAKER, JOKER, NEUTRAL, PENDING, SUSPECT, UNKNOWN): 

ASSUMED FRIEND: Track assumed to be a friend due to the object characteristics, behavior, and/or origin.

FRIEND: Track object supporting friendly forces and belonging to a declared friendly nation or entity.

HOSTILE: Track object belonging to an opposing nation, party, group, or entity deemed to contribute to a threat to friendly forces or their mission due to its behavior, characteristics, nationality, or origin.

FAKER: Friendly track, object, or entity acting as an exercise hostile.

JOKER: Friendly track, object, or entity acting as an exercise suspect.

NEUTRAL: Track object whose characteristics, behavior, nationality, and/or origin indicate that it is neither supporting nor opposing friendly forces or their mission.

PENDING: Track object which has not been evaluated.

SUSPECT: Track object deemed potentially hostile due to the object characteristics, behavior, nationality, and/or origin.

UNKNOWN: Track object which has been evaluated and does not meet criteria for any standard identity.

allegiance.description: The DoD Standard country code designator for the country or political entity to which the operating unit owes its allegiance.  This field will be set to "OTHR" if the source value does not match a UDL country code value (ISO-3166-ALPHA-2).

altAllegiance.description: Specifies an alternate allegiance code if the data provider code is not part of an official Country Code standard such as ISO-3166 or FIPS. This field will be set to the value provided by the source and should be used for all Queries specifying allegiance.

locReason.description: Indicates the reason that the operating unit is at that location.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

force.description: An aggregation of military units within a single service (i.e., ARMY, AIR FORCE, etc.) which operates under a single authority to accomplish a common mission. The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

forceName.description: The specific name for a given force.  For example, Force = ADF (Air Defense Force) and Force Name = Army Air Defense Force.

functRole.description: Principal combat-related role that an operating unit is organized, structured and equipped to perform.  Or, the specialized military or paramilitary branch in which an individual serves, their specialization.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

msnPrimary.description: Indicates the principal type of mission that an operating unit is organized and equipped to perform.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

msnPrimarySpecialty.description: Indicates the principal specialty type of mission that an operating unit is organized and equipped to perform.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

masterUnit.description: This field contains a value indicating whether the record is a master unit record (True) or a detail record (False).  Master records contain basic information that does not change over time for each unit that has been selected to be projected.

stylizedUnit.description: This field contains a value indicating whether the record is a stylized operating unit record (True) or a regular operating unit  record (False).  A stylized operating unit is a type of operating unit with one set of equipment that can be assigned to one or more superiors.  A stylized operating unit is generally useful for lower echelon operating units where the number of operating units and types of equipment are equal for multiple organizations.  In lieu of creating unique operating unit records for each operating unit, a template is created for the operating unit and its equipment.  This template enables the user to assign the operating unit to multiple organizations.

divCat.description: Combat status of a divisional or equivalent operating unit.  Currently, this data element applies only to operating units of the Former Soviet Union.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

echelon.description: Organizational level of the operating unit.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

echelonTier.description: Indicates the major group or level to which an echelon belongs.   The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

fleetId.description: Naval fleet to which an operating unit is assigned.   The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

deployStatus.description: A code describing the amount of operating unit participation in a deployment.   The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

flagFlown.description: The country code of the observed flag flown.

coordDatum.description: A mathematical model of the earth used to calculate coordinates on a map.  US Forces use the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84), but also use maps by allied countries with local datums.  The datum must be specified to ensure accuracy of coordinates.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

coord.description:
Indicates any of the magnitudes that serve to define the position of a point by reference to a fixed figure, system of lines, etc.

Pos. 1-2. Latitude Degrees     [00-90]

Pos. 3-4. Latitude Minutes     [00-59]

Pos. 5-6. Latitude Seconds     [00-59]

Pos. 7-9. Latitude Thousandths Of Seconds     [000-999]

Pos. 10. Latitude Hemisphere     [NS]

Pos. 11-13. Longitude Degrees     [00-180]

Pos. 14-15. Longitude Minutes     [00-59]

Pos. 16-17. Longitude Seconds     [00-59]

Pos. 18-20. Longitude Thousandths Of Seconds     [000-999]

Pos. 21. Longitude Hemisphere     [EW]

Pos. 1-21. Unknown Latitude and Unknown Longitude     [000000000U000000000U]

coordDerivAcc.description: Indicates the plus or minus error assessed against the method used to derive the coordinate.

lat.description: WGS84 latitude of the location, in degrees. -90 to 90 degrees (negative values south of equator).

lon.description: WGS84 longitude of the location, in degrees. -180 to 180 degrees (negative values west of Prime Meridian).

elevMsl.description: Ground elevation of the geographic coordinates referenced to (above or below) Mean Sea Level (MSL) vertical datum.

elevMslConfLvl.description: Indicates the confidence level expressed as a percent that a specific geometric spatial element, ELEVATION_MSL linear accuracy, has been vertically positioned to within a specified vertical accuracy.

elevMslDerivAcc.description: Indicates the plus or minus error assessed against the method used to derive the elevation.

geoidalMslSep.description: The distance between Mean Sea Level and a referenced ellipsoid.

milGridSys.description:
Indicates the grid system used in the development of the milGrid coordinates. Values are:

UPS - Universal Polar System

UTM - Universal Transverse Mercator

milGrid.description:
The Military Grid Reference System is the geocoordinate standard used by NATO militaries for locating points on Earth. The MGRS is derived from the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) grid system and the Universal Polar Stereographic (UPS) grid system, but uses a different labeling convention. The MGRS is used as geocode for the entire Earth. Example of an milgrid coordinate, or grid reference, would be 4QFJ12345678, which consists of three parts:
4Q (grid zone designator, GZD)
FJ (the 100,000-meter square identifier)
12345678 (numerical location; easting is 1234 and northing is 5678, in this case specifying a location with 10 m resolution).

utm.description:
Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) grid coordinates.
Pos. 1-2, UTM Zone Column   [01-60
Pos. 3, UTM Zone Row   [C-HJ-NP-X]
Pos. 4, UTM False Easting   [0-9]
Pos. 5-9, UTM Meter Easting    [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]
Pos. 10-11, UTM False Northing    [0-9][0-9]
Pos. 12-16, UTM Meter Northing    [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9].

airDefArea.description: Air Defense District (ADD) or Air Defense Area (ADA) in which the geographic coordinates reside.

polSubdiv.description: Political subdivision in which the geographic coordinates reside.  The specific usage and enumerations contained in this field may be found in the documentation provided in the referenceDoc field.  If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

symCode.description: A standard scheme for symbol coding enabling the transfer, display and use of symbols and graphics among information systems, as per MIL-STD 2525B, and supported by the element AFFILIATION.

classRating.description:
Indicates the importance of the operating unit to the OES or MIR system.  This data element is restricted to update by DIA (DB-4). Valid values are:
0 - Does not meet criteria above
1 - Primary importance to system
2 - Secondary importance to system
3 - Tertiary importance to system
O - Other. Explain in Remarks.

recStatus.description:
Validity and currency of the data in the record to be used in conjunction with the other elements in the record as defined by SOPs. Values are:
A - Active
I - Inactive
K - Acknowledged
L - Local
Q - A nominated (NOM) or Data Change Request (DCR) record
R - Production reduced by CMD decision
W - Working Record.

reviewDate.description: Date on which the data in the record was last reviewed by the responsible analyst for accuracy and currency.  This date cannot be greater than the current date.

resProd.description: Responsible Producer - Organization that is responsible for the maintenance of the record.

referenceDoc.description: The reference documentiation that specifies the usage and enumerations contained in this record. If referenceDoc not provided, users may consult the data provider.

createdAt.description: Time the row was created in the database, auto-populated by the system.

createdBy.description: Application user who created the row in the database, auto-populated by the system.

origin.description: Originating system or organization which produced the data, if different from the source. The origin may be different than the source if the source was a mediating system which forwarded the data on behalf of the origin system. If null, the source may be assumed to be the origin.

OpticalSOIObservation_Full.description: An Optical SOI record contains observation information taken from a sensor about a Space Object.

obStartTime.description: Observation detection start time in ISO 8601 UTC with microsecond precision.

intensityTimes.description: Array of start times for each intensity measurement. The 1st value in the array will match obStartTime.

currentSpectralFilterNum.description: The reference number, x, where x ranges from 1 to n, where n is the number specified in spectralFilters that corresponds to the spectral filter used.

intensities.description: Array of intensities of the Space Object for observations, in kilowatts per steradian per micrometer.

extinctionCoeffs.description: Array of coefficients for how much signal would be lost to atmospheric attenuation for a star at zenith for each element in intensities, in magnitudes per air mass.

extinctionCoeffsUnc.description: Array of extinction coefficient uncertainties for each element in intensities. Each value represents the difference between the measured brightness and predicted brightness of the star with the extinction removed, making it exo-atmospheric (e.g. -5.0 to 30.0).

skyBgs.description: Array of average Sky Background signals, in magnitudes, with a value corresponding to the time of each intensity measurement. Sky Background refers to the incoming light from an apparently empty part of the night sky.

localSkyBgs.description: Array of local average Sky Background signals, in magnitudes, with a value corresponding to the time of each intensity measurement. Sky Background refers to the incoming light from an apparently empty part of the night sky.

localSkyBgsUnc.description: Array of uncertainty of the local average Sky Background signal, in magnitudes, with a value corresponding to the time of each intensity measurement.

numDetectedStars.description: Array of the number of detected stars in the FOV with a value for each element in the intensities field.

numCorrelatedStars.description: Array of the number of correlated stars in the FOV with a value for each element in the intensities field.

zeroPoints.description: Array of values for the zero-point in magnitudes, calculated at the time of each intensity measurement. It is the difference between the catalog mag and instrumental mag for a set of standard stars (e.g. -5.0 to 30.0).

ras.description: Array of right ascension values, in degrees, of the Target object from the frame of reference of the sensor. A value is provided for each element in the intensities field.

declinations.description: Array of declination values, in degrees, of the Target object from the frame of reference of the sensor. A value is provided for each element in the intensities field, at the middle of the frame’s exposure time.

raRates.description: Array of right ascension rate values, in degrees per second, measuring the rate the telescope is moving to track the Target object from the frame of reference of the sensor, for each element in the intensities field, at the middle of the frame’s exposure time.

declinationRates.description: Array of declination rate values, in degrees per second, measuring the rate speed at which an object's declination changes over time, for each element in the intensities field, at the middle of the frame's exposure time.

percentSats.description: Array of values giving the percent of pixels that make up the object signal that are beyond the saturation point for the sensor, with a value for each element in the intensities field.
